summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for evaluation of progressive dyspnea and symptomatic anemia with hemoglobin of 6.5 g/dL. He was found to have a 2.5 cm gastric polyp in the incisura, which biopsy confirmed as poorly differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma. He underwent endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) without complications. Staging CT showed no metastatic disease. His anticoagulation was managed with heparin bridging during the procedure, and warfarin was resumed with INR 2.5 at discharge. Heart failure was managed conservatively, with temporary discontinuation of torsemide due to acute kidney injury from contrast. His cirrhosis was stable, and he was discharged home with plans for oncology, hepatology, and primary care follow-up, along with outpatient lab monitoring.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of lesser curvature of stomach, unspecified
Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
